explanations: luna: The section makes a furnished garden room the pattern for a furnished world; here Allah calls earth a bed, فِرَاشًا, and sky a building, بِنَاءً, stating that room and world relation directly. | terra: The section reads earth and sky as the floor and roof of one furnished world; this ayah makes the earth a bed (فِرَاشًا) and the sky a building, stating that domestic architecture directly.
terra: The section pairs furnishing the earth with proportioning the high sky; this ayah first provides all that is on earth and then forms the heavens into seven.
terra: The world-image gives sky and mountain distinct jobs as roof and peg; this ayah raises Mount above the covenant people, making the mountain occupy the canopy's position.
terra: As in 2:63, Mount is raised over the people; that exceptional scene reverses the section's normal arrangement of mountain fixed below and sky raised above.

luna: The section's root reading of ر ف ع includes raising a building; Abraham and Ishmael raise the House's foundations, showing the same upward building action at human scale. | terra: The section explains رفع as raising a construction; this ayah shows Abraham and Ishmael raising the foundations of the House, a literal building use of the same gesture.

luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث links a spread carpet with living things spread on earth; this verse says Allah dispersed every kind of creature there, making the laid-out world inhabited. | terra: The section hears مَبْثُوثَةٌ as both carpets spread and living beings broadcast on earth; this ayah places that broadcasting of every creature inside a detailed heavens-and-earth sign scene.
terra: The section raises roofs and arranges a habitable room; this ayah confronts a town fallen in upon its roofs, then uses its revival as a sign of resurrection.
terra: The section extends measured creation from world to human form; this ayah says God shapes people in the wombs however He wills, a hidden instance of the same fitting craft.
terra: Placed cups become part of a larger account of things and spaces set down for inhabitants; this ayah calls the first House the one placed (وُضِعَ) for humankind.
terra: The prose uses بث for both spreading rugs and spreading creatures; this ayah uses the same act for broadcasting many men and women from one pair across the human world.
terra: This ayah repeats the covenant scene in which Mount is raised over the people, again placing the mountain where the section normally places the canopy.

terra: The section defines نصب as setting a protruding object upright and applies it to God's mountains; this ayah condemns humanly erected cult stones (الْأَنْصَابُ), a contrary use of the physical gesture.
terra: The section bases the world's made order on measure; this ayah makes night a repose and the sun and moon a means of calculation, giving the inhabited cosmos temporal measure.
terra: The section furnishes the Garden with raised seating and makes earth a bed beneath a roof; this ayah gives Hell a bed with coverings above, a direct infernal reversal of that habitable room.

terra: The section makes room and landscape two scales of one craft; this ayah says Thamud made palaces on the plains and carved houses from the mountains, bringing ground, mountain, and dwelling into one construction scene.

luna: The section sets mountains in the earth and the sky above as canopy; here the mountain is lifted over a people like a shade, كَأَنَّهُ ظُلَّةٌ, reversing the mountain's place in that room-and-world arrangement. | terra: The section's mountains are upright pegs beneath a roof; this ayah raises the mountain above the people like a canopy, deliberately exchanging the two cosmic roles.

terra: The section grounds skilled making in straightness and sound measure; this ayah contrasts a building founded on reverence with one built on a crumbling edge that collapses with its builder into fire.
terra: The section finds exact proportion beneath creation; this ayah determines measured stations for the moon so people can know years and reckoning, an ordered celestial counterpart.
terra: The section's command to look moves across camel, sky, mountains, and earth; this ayah commands people to look at what is in the heavens and earth, giving the same stance its widest field.
terra: The section has raised couches; this ayah performs the closely corresponding action when Joseph raises his parents onto the throne, joining physical elevation to furnished seating.

luna: The section's dictionary image makes the raised sky a tent canopy whose pole is absent; this ayah says the heavens were raised بِغَيْرِ عَمَدٍ تَرَوْنَهَا, letting the roof stand without visible supports. | terra: The section imagines a tent-like world with a raised roof and discusses its pole; this ayah says God raised the heavens without visible pillars, directly marking the absent supports.

luna: Allah spreads the earth and sets firm mountains and rivers in it; the floor and upright mountain arrangement matches the section's world furnishing. | terra: The section's world is made by spreading ground and fixing mountains into it; this ayah joins the extended earth with firm mountains, rivers, and paired fruits.
terra: In the context of what wombs bear, diminish, and increase, this ayah says every thing with God is according to a measure, extending the section's craft-measure into hidden growth.

terra: The section presents the current earth and sky as a completed room; this ayah marks the Day when earth is exchanged for another earth and the heavens also, setting a boundary on that construction.
terra: The section turns the made world into a furnished space offered to sight; this ayah places constellations in the sky and adorns it for those who look.

luna: Earth is spread, mountains set firmly, and balanced growth brought forth there; this gives the section's level floor and planted supports a productive landscape. | terra: The section makes straight measure, an extended floor, and upright mountains aspects of one craft; this ayah joins earth spread out, firm mountains set in it, and everything grown there in due measure.

luna: The section's dictionary reading of creation as measured workmanship meets this ayah's بِقَدَرٍ مَعْلُومٍ, a known measure for what is sent down. | terra: The section treats the made world as both measured and furnished; this ayah says that nothing is sent from God's treasuries except in a known measure, connecting provision to exact apportionment.

luna: The section's cushions and couches furnish a garden room; this verse places reconciled brothers on couches facing one another, إِخْوَانًا عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ, a direct social use of the same furniture. | terra: The section's room is arranged for repose; this ayah places the Garden's purified companions as brothers on couches facing one another.
terra: The section moves between a prepared room and erected mountains; this ayah has Thamud carve secure houses out of the mountains themselves.

terra: The section begins the made world with the camel and later hears rugs of hair and wool; this ayah says God created livestock for warmth, benefits, and food, supplying the animal material side of that craft.

luna: The verse says mountains were set in the earth so it would not sway; this makes the section's mountain-as-peg image explain the world's stability. | terra: The prose treats mountains as planted pegs that make the earth fit; this ayah says God cast firm mountains into earth so that it would not sway with its inhabitants.
terra: The section's world depends on an elevated roof and upright construction; this ayah has God strike a building at its foundations so that its roof falls upon its makers.
terra: The section joins creature, mountain, tent, and house; this ayah directs the bee to take houses in mountains, trees, and human trellises, another meeting of habitation with the made landscape.

terra: The section hears a tent in the raised sky, pegged mountains, and spread ground, and notes a thick rug of camel hair or wool; this ayah joins hide tents with wool, fur, and hair furnishings, making the room-world analogy materially exact.
terra: After 16:80 gives hide tents and animal-hair furnishings, this ayah gives shade and shelters in the mountains, extending the made world's protection from room to landscape.

luna: In this garden, people recline on couches amid silk and ornaments; it turns the section's listed couches into an inhabited paradise setting. | terra: The prepared room becomes inhabited here: Garden-dwellers recline on couches amid flowing rivers, showing the use of the seating listed in the section.

luna: The section presents mountains set in place and an exposed, spread earth; here mountains are made to move and earth is laid bare at gathering, reversing that settled landscape. | terra: The section fixes mountains upright over a spread earth; this ayah moves the mountains away and leaves the earth exposed, dismantling both parts of that arrangement.
terra: The prose defines صف as setting things on one straight line; this ayah presents humanity before its Lord in a row, applying the same arrangement to persons rather than cushions.
terra: The section treats upright setting as a builder's action; this ayah has the servant straighten or restore a wall about to collapse, a small-scale instance of making structure stand.
terra: The section links upright construction to straightness; this ayah has the barrier raised between mountain sides until the iron mass is made level with them, then finished with molten copper.
terra: The section treats creation as giving each thing a measured, fitting form; this ayah says that the Lord gave every thing its creation and then guided it, joining form to function.

luna: Allah makes earth a cradle, مَهْدًا, and lays out paths in it; this presents the section's spread floor as a fitted place for human travel. | terra: The section's earth is a laid and livable surface; this ayah says God made it a cradle or bed for people and traced roads through it.
terra: The prose defines صف as arranging things on one straight line; this ayah tells Pharaoh's magicians to assemble their scheme and then come in a single row.

luna: The section shows mountains erected as supports; here the Lord says He will blow them away, يَنسِفُهَا رَبِّي نَسْفًا, reversing their planted stability. | terra: The section's mountains are erected as the world's pegs; this ayah answers the question about them by saying God will pulverize them, preparing the level plain of 20:106.

luna: The section's source lexicon uses صَفْصَف for level land; after 20:105 removes the mountains, this ayah leaves a level plain, قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا, turning the pegs into bare floor. | terra: The prose explicitly derives صَفْصَف from the straight row and applies it to level land; after 20:105 removes the mountains, this ayah leaves the ground a bare level plain (قَاعًا صَفْصَفًا), a Last-Day reversal of the furnished world.

luna: This continues the level plain of 20:106, with no crookedness or unevenness; the emptied ground completes the reversal of the section's furnished, shaped world. | terra: After 20:105 removes the mountains and 20:106 leaves a level plain, this ayah says no curvature or unevenness will be seen there, completing the reversal of pegged, articulated terrain.

luna: Firm mountains are placed so the earth will not shake with its inhabitants; the verse supplies the stabilizing purpose behind the section's upright mountains. | terra: The section erects mountains within a stable floor; this ayah places firm mountains in earth so it will not shake with people, explaining a function of the pegs.

luna: The section's dictionary describes the sky as a roof; here it is made a protected roof, سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا, directly turning that secondary sense into a cosmic image. | terra: The prose defines the sky through a house roof; this ayah explicitly makes the sky a protected roof (سَقْفًا مَحْفُوظًا).
terra: The section's constructed cosmos rests on ordered measure; this ayah creates night, day, sun, and moon and gives each its own swimming course.
terra: The section links the act of placing with measure through the placed balance; this ayah places just balances for the Resurrection, extending that ordered gesture to exact judgment.

luna: The section imagines the sky as a raised canopy; here the heavens are folded like a written scroll, a specific reversal of that stretched roof. | terra: The section unfolds the sky as a high roof; this ayah folds that sky like a written scroll, reversing the gesture by which the world-room was opened and raised.

luna: The section places the camel beside cushions aligned in a row; here sacrificial camels stand صَوَافَّ, joining its animal and alignment images while adding the distinct setting of sacrifice. | terra: The section joins the camel with the straight row of cushions; this ayah brings those details together in sacrificial camels standing in orderly rows (صَوَافَّ).
terra: The section's roof is raised over an inhabited floor; this ayah evokes destroyed settlements whose buildings have collapsed upon their roofs, reversing the stable room-form.
terra: The section asks how the sky stays raised as the world's roof; this ayah says God holds the sky back from falling upon earth except by permission.

terra: The section presents creation as a sequence of fitted acts; this ayah narrates successive transformations from drop through bones and flesh to another creation, then praises the best of creators.
terra: The section's craft depends on right measure and a prepared earth; this ayah sends water down in measure and settles it in the earth, joining measurement to placement in the world.
terra: The prose explains بث as spreading created beings through earth; with a different verb, this ayah says God multiplied or dispersed people in earth and will gather them back to Him.

luna: The section's root reading of ر ف ع includes raising buildings; this ayah uses تُرْفَعَ for houses set apart for remembrance, a human-scale instance of the same raised structure. | terra: The section notes that رفع is used for building upward; this ayah speaks of houses God permitted to be raised, while its context also permits the sense of honoring them.

luna: The section's dictionary entry gives measuring as a secondary sense of خَلَقَ; this ayah says Allah created all things and determined them precisely, فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا. | terra: The prose recovers measuring as the first act of creation; this ayah joins creating every thing to determining it with exact determination (فَقَدَّرَهُ تَقْدِيرًا).
terra: The section reads the sky as a prepared ceiling; this ayah places constellations in the sky and sets within it a lamp and illuminating moon, furnishing that ceiling with lights.
terra: The section's Garden interior is high and prepared for its inhabitants; this ayah rewards the patient with the lofty chamber and a greeting of peace.
terra: Against the section's purposeful measured construction, this ayah rebukes building a monument on every height merely in play, distinguishing skilled form from purposeless display.
terra: Continuing 26:128's rebuke, this ayah faults the making of massive structures as though their builders would live forever, exposing the false permanence of worldly construction.
terra: The room-world image meets at the mountain here: the people carve houses skillfully or proudly from mountains, applying deliberate workmanship to the section's great upright objects.

terra: The section compares a leveled world-surface with a laid room-floor; this ayah presents a palace paved smooth with glass that is mistaken for natural water, deliberately blurring constructed interior and landscape.
terra: The section reads land, mountains, and a made dwelling together; this ayah makes earth a stable abode and gives it rivers, firm mountains, and a barrier between seas.

luna: The section asks how mountains are set up; this verse says they seem fixed while they pass like clouds, exposing the boundary of that apparent stability. | terra: The section's erected mountains seem to be the fixed workmanship of the world; this ayah says they appear rigid yet pass like clouds, while naming God's craft that perfects every thing.
terra: The section commands attention to how the camel and world were created; this ayah commands travel through the earth and looking at how creation was begun.
terra: The section furnishes the Garden as a dwelling; this ayah promises believers chambers in the Garden with rivers below, where they remain.
terra: The prose pairs creation with living beings spread on earth; this ayah says God created humans from dust and then they became people dispersing across the earth.
luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث links a spread surface with dispersed creatures; here rain revives earth and Allah disperses creatures through the two realms.

luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث links carpets spread out with creatures spread through the land; this ayah also places anchored mountains and a pillarless sky around that dispersed life. | terra: The section joins a pillarless sky, set mountains, and creatures spread across earth; this ayah contains all three: heavens without visible pillars, firm mountains, and every creature broadcast on earth.
terra: The prose treats creation as competent, straight workmanship; this ayah says God made excellent every thing He created, stating the quality implied by the four careful gestures.
terra: Following 32:7-8's account of excellent creation, this ayah says God proportioned the human being and breathed into him, supplying the finishing act of that craft.
terra: The section lists four objects marked by the work performed on them; this ayah likewise lists chambers, statues, basin-like dishes, and fixed cauldrons as things craftsmen make for Solomon.
terra: The section's raised room belongs to final security; this ayah says those brought near are secure in the Garden's chambers.

luna: Allah holds the heavens and earth lest they slip away; this adds the sustaining force behind the section's roof-and-floor world. | terra: The constructed world in the section depends on sustained placement; this ayah says God holds the heavens and earth lest they cease or slip away.
terra: The section grounds cosmic making in exact measure; this ayah describes the sun running to an appointed point and calls that the determination of the Mighty, Knowing.
terra: Alongside the sun's determination in 36:38, this ayah says God measured stages for the moon, another explicit act of fitting the sky's contents to order.
terra: This ayah distinguishes the courses of sun, moon, night, and day and gives each an orbit, spelling out the non-overlap produced by the measurement in 36:38-39.

luna: People and their spouses recline on couches in the garden; this shows the section's couches as part of a social, lived-in room. | terra: The section lists the still furnishings of a Garden room; this ayah places the Garden-dwellers and their spouses reclining on couches in shade.
terra: The section's first world-object is the created camel and it speaks of a maker's hand movements; this ayah asks whether people see the livestock created for them by what God's hands made.
terra: After 36:71 calls livestock a work made for humans, this ayah says God subjected them so some are mounts and some food, answering in part what their created form is fitted to do.

luna: The section's root ص ف ف describes placing things in a straight line; this oath pictures beings lined up in ranks, وَالصَّافَّاتِ صَفًّا. | terra: The cushions' صف is an orderly line; this oath by those ranged in ranks transfers that exact spatial order to a living host.

luna: The section treats the raised sky as the world's roof; this ayah says the nearest sky is adorned with stars, adding a specific decoration to that overhead scene. | terra: The section moves from a made room to a made sky; this ayah describes the nearest sky as adorned with stars, a cosmic counterpart to furnishing an interior.

luna: The people in this garden sit عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مُّتَقَابِلِينَ, on couches facing one another; it adds the companionship and orientation that make the section's furniture a setting. | terra: The section's raised couches form a social room; this ayah seats the honored servants on couches facing one another.

luna: The section's cups are placed in a furnished garden; this neighboring ayah to 37:44 shows a cup from a flowing spring being circulated among those seated there. | terra: The section has cups already placed in the Garden room; here a cup from a flowing spring is circulated among the reclining blessed, showing that prepared vessel in use.
terra: The section's straight arrangement of furnishings has a living counterpart here, where the angels say that they themselves are those who stand in ordered rows.
terra: The section's raised furniture opens onto an architectural Garden; this ayah promises chambers above which are further chambers, all built, giving vertical form to the prepared dwelling.

terra: The section describes the world through a maker's hand movements; this ayah has the whole earth grasped and the heavens folded in God's right hand on the Last Day, an answering gesture of dismantling.

luna: Allah makes earth a place of rest and sky a building, then shapes people well and provides good things; this gathers the section's floor, roof, and fitted creation into one account. | terra: The section sees the world as a habitable room and creation as skilled shaping; this ayah makes earth a settled place, sky a building, and human forms beautiful in one account.
luna: Before 41:10 places mountains and apportions provision, this ayah says the earth was created in two days; it supplies the opening stage of the measured construction sequence.

luna: The verse sets mountains above the earth and apportions its provisions in measured days; it joins the section's planted landscape to its claim that making is measured. | terra: The section connects raised mountains and exact measure in making the world fit; this ayah sets firm mountains above the earth and measures its provisions.
terra: Before 41:12 orders the sky into seven heavens and adorns the nearest one, this ayah addresses the smoke-like sky and earth and records their willing submission to being formed.

luna: The heavens are completed as seven and the nearest sky adorned with lamps; this adds a decorated ceiling to the section's constructed cosmos. | terra: Following the sky's submission to shaping in 41:11, this ayah orders it as seven heavens and adorns the nearest one with lamps, adding furnishing to construction.

luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث joins spread rugs to spread creatures; this ayah says creatures are dispersed through heavens and earth, making the world floor part of a populated design. | terra: The prose explicitly links creation to broadcasting living beings over the made world; this ayah joins creation of the heavens and earth with the creatures God has spread through them.

luna: Allah makes earth a cradle, مَهْدًا, and puts paths through it; this is another direct picture of the earth as a fitted surface. | terra: Like the section's prepared ground, this ayah makes earth a cradle or bed for its addressees and places paths in it for guidance.

luna: This ayah pictures silver roofs over earthly houses, سَقْفًا مِّن فِضَّةٍ; the section's raised sky is a cosmic roof, while 43:35 calls such wealth worldly enjoyment, adding a temporal boundary to the furnished-world image.

luna: This ayah adds doors and couches people recline upon in the same earthly houses; 43:35 frames that luxury as worldly enjoyment, a boundary alongside the section's garden couches. | terra: The Garden's couches and the world's furnished rooms meet here in doors and couches made for unbelievers' houses; 43:35 limits all of it to temporary worldly enjoyment.
terra: After 43:33-34 imagine silver roofs, stairs, doors, and couches, this ayah calls all such furnishing only the enjoyment of the nearer life and reserves the final abode for the reverent.
terra: Immediately before the vessels and cups of 43:71, this ayah admits the faithful and their spouses into the Garden rejoicing, identifying the inhabitants for whom that hospitality is arranged.

luna: Golden trays and cups are circulated among the people of the garden; the placed cups of the section become part of an active feast. | terra: The section's placed cups become active hospitality here as golden trays and cups are circulated around the Garden-dwellers.

luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث connects spread rugs and spread life; this verse calls human creation and the creatures Allah disperses signs to reflect on. | terra: The section connects a created creature with living beings spread through the world; this ayah makes both human creation and the creatures God continually disperses signs for certainty.

luna: The question أَفَلَمْ يَنظُرُوا invites people to look at the built and adorned sky above them; it echoes the section's call to inspect how the sky is raised. | terra: The section asks people to look at how the sky was raised; this ayah likewise asks whether they have looked at the sky above, then names its building, adornment, and lack of fissures.

luna: Allah spreads the earth and casts firm mountains into it; this closely repeats the section's ground-and-mountain construction image. | terra: The section's ground is spread and its mountains erected as fixed features; this ayah likewise joins earth extended with firm mountains cast into it.

luna: The sky is built and made vast, بَنَيْنَاهَا بِأَيْدٍ وَإِنَّا لَمُوسِعُونَ; this gives the section's raised canopy an explicit act of cosmic building. | terra: Where the section treats the sky as a raised roof made by a craftsman's gesture, this ayah says that God built the sky with power, supplying the construction half of the same room-world pair.

luna: The section's root reading for the spread carpet is echoed in Allah's words وَالْأَرْضَ فَرَشْنَاهَا; the earth itself is laid out as a floor covering. | terra: The section's level earth is also a laid carpet; this ayah says the earth was spread as a bed and praises its Maker as the excellent spreader.
terra: Immediately before the oath by the raised roof in 52:5, this ayah swears by the inhabited House, sharpening the section's reading of that roof as part of a dwelling.

luna: The verse swears by the raised roof, السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ; the section's dictionary sense of sky as a roof becomes a direct Qur'anic image. | terra: The section explicitly hears the sky as the roof of a house; this oath to the raised roof (السَّقْفِ الْمَرْفُوعِ) condenses that cosmic architecture.
terra: The same surah swears by the raised roof in 52:5; this ayah shows the sky convulsing on the promised Day, undoing that stable ceiling.

luna: The section's roof and mountains are settled structures; this Day of Judgment scene says the mountains move, unsettling the fitted landscape. | terra: Alongside the shaking sky of 52:9, the mountains move away here; the surah later answers that dismantled world with the lined Garden couches of 52:20.

luna: The section's root ص ف ف describes cushions aligned in a straight row; here the garden's couches are مَصْفُوفَةً, giving the same ordered furniture arrangement. | terra: The section's Garden room contains couches and a straight row; this ayah reunites the same details in couches set in rows (سُرُرٍ مَصْفُوفَةٍ) on which the blessed recline.

luna: After the couches of 52:20, this ayah has garden dwellers pass a cup among themselves, كَأْسًا; it shows how a cup in the section's room is used in company. | terra: The section supplies cups as part of the room; this ayah shows the inhabitants passing a cup among one another without the corrupting speech or sin of earthly drinking.

luna: The section's dictionary reading connects creation with correct measure; this ayah says every thing was created بِقَدَرٍ, making measured workmanship explicit. | terra: The section develops خَلْق as straight and exact measuring before a thing is made; this ayah declares that every thing is created according to a measure.
terra: Before the sky is raised and the balance placed in 55:7, this ayah says the sun and moon run by calculation, giving cosmic motion the same exact order the section finds in cosmic construction.

luna: The section calls attention to lifting and placing; here Allah raises the sky and places the balance, رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ, joining those actions in one created order. | terra: The section emphasizes that raising and placing belong to one furnishing sequence; this ayah puts them side by side in the raised sky and the placed balance (رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ الْمِيزَانَ).

luna: This ayah continues the balance placed in 55:7 by warning people not to transgress the scale; the section's measured craft thus opens onto the limits of human measure. | terra: The placed balance in 55:7 extends the section's right measure into conduct; this ayah makes the consequence explicit by forbidding transgression in the balance.

luna: After the balance in 55:7 and warning in 55:8, this ayah orders just weight; it gives the section's measured order a human practice as well. | terra: The section roots making in straight measure; this ayah commands establishing weight with justice and not making the balance deficient, turning crafted evenness into moral evenness.

luna: The section's root reading of وَضَعَ includes setting an object in place; this ayah says Allah placed the earth for all creatures, وَالْأَرْضَ وَضَعَهَا لِلْأَنَامِ. | terra: The section moves from objects placed in a room to the earth laid out for living creatures; this ayah says that the earth itself was placed for all creatures.
terra: Earlier this surah raises the sky and places the earth; here the sky is split and becomes rose-red like oil or hide, marking the end of the constructed canopy.

luna: Garden dwellers recline on richly lined couches with fruit close at hand; this gives the section's furnishings their setting and use. | terra: The section's array of Garden furnishings is matched by this scene of reclining on beds whose inner linings are brocade, adding the tactile construction of the bedding.

luna: The section's dictionary image compares the world to a tent; this verse places garden companions in pavilions, الْخِيَامِ, a literal tent-like dwelling within paradise. | terra: The prose's world resembles a tent while its room belongs to the Garden; this ayah places secluded companions in Garden tents, bringing the two spatial images together.

luna: The section names cushions and rugs as furnishings; this garden has green cushions, رَفْرَفٍ خُضْرٍ, and fine carpets, عَبْقَرِيٍّ حِسَانٍ, a direct furnishing parallel. | terra: The section ends its room-list with spread carpets and cushions; this ayah seats the Garden-dwellers on green cushions or spreads and beautiful carpets.

terra: The section's raised furnishings and high Garden give elevation a physical form; this ayah calls the Event both abasing and raising, transferring the same vertical opposition to final destinies.
luna: The section's earth is laid out as a stable floor; here earth is shaken violently, reversing its settled surface.

luna: The section's mountains stand as placed supports; here they are crushed, بُسَّتِ الْجِبَالُ بَسًّا, and lose that form. | terra: The section erects mountains as stable pegs; this ayah crushes them completely, and 56:6 turns their remains into dispersed dust.

terra: The section's carpets are مَبْثُوثَةٌ in orderly abundance; after the mountains are crushed in 56:5, this ayah makes them scattered dust (هَبَاءً مُنْبَثًّا), reversing furnishing into dispersal.

luna: This garden's couches are woven or inlaid, سُرُرٍ مَوْضُونَةٍ; the detail expands the section's list of crafted furnishings. | terra: The section's elevated seating belongs to an ordered Garden interior; this ayah introduces elaborately woven or arrayed couches.

luna: The ayah continues the couches of 56:15 and seats their occupants facing each other; it adds a social arrangement to the section's ordered room. | terra: This ayah supplies the posture and relation for the couches named in 56:15: the blessed recline on them facing one another, as in the section's prepared room.
terra: The section's cups are set ready; this ayah introduces immortal youths circulating among the blessed, and 56:18 names the vessels they carry.

luna: After the couches and facing guests of 56:15–16, this ayah names cups and pitchers from a flowing spring; it extends the furnished scene to the section's placed cups. | terra: Continuing 56:17, this ayah names goblets, pitchers, and a cup from a flowing spring, closely expanding the section's single placed-cup image.

luna: The verse names raised couches, فُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ; it matches the section's root ر ف ع and its lifted garden furniture. | terra: The section's couches are raised; this ayah gives the nearest Garden furnishing parallel in raised beds (فُرُشٍ مَرْفُوعَةٍ).
terra: Immediately after the raised beds of 56:34, this ayah says the Garden companions were brought forth in a special creation, meeting the furnished room with a new act of making.

luna: The section explicitly cites the balance placed with the raised sky in 55:7; this ayah again pairs the revealed balance with people establishing justice, الْمِيزَانَ لِيَقُومَ النَّاسُ بِالْقِسْطِ.

terra: The section imagines the maker's hand arranging and raising a dwelling; this ayah has people ruin their own houses with their hands and the believers' hands, turning the handwork of habitation into dismantling.
terra: The section unfolds creation through measuring, shaping, and setting in order; this ayah gathers the divine names Creator, Originator, and Former, distinguishing those aspects of making.

luna: The section's root ص ف ف describes things aligned in a straight row; this verse praises people standing in ranks like a compact structure, صَفًّا كَأَنَّهُم بُنْيَانٌ مَّرْصُوصٌ. | terra: The prose defines a row as placing things on one straight line and repeatedly compares furnishing to building; this ayah combines both images in a rank like a compact structure.
terra: The section joins the true construction of heavens and earth to the proportioning of creatures; this ayah creates both in truth and then forms human beings beautifully.
terra: The section says that making begins with due measure; in a promise about trust and provision, this ayah says God has appointed a measure for every thing.
terra: The section furnishes a room in the Garden; Pharaoh's wife asks God here to build for her, near Him, a house in the Garden, directly joining divine building, room, and final abode.

luna: The sky is created in layers with no mismatch; this makes the section's raised ceiling a deliberately ordered construction. | terra: The section asks the hearer to inspect a made sky and its even order; this ayah describes layered heavens with no disparity and commands the gaze to search for a fissure.

luna: After 67:3 describes the layered sky, this ayah tells the viewer to look again for flaws; it echoes the section's invitation to inspect the created world. | terra: This ayah repeats the inspecting gaze begun in 67:3 until it returns defeated, turning the section's question about how things were made into a sustained test of their flawless measure.

luna: The section's sky-as-roof image receives a parallel adornment here: the nearest sky is decorated with lamps, مَصَابِيحَ, continuing the crafted-ceiling image. | terra: After the measured layered heavens of 67:3, this ayah says the nearest heaven was adorned with lamps, showing the raised canopy also furnished with light.
terra: The section's flattened earth is made usable for its inhabitants; this ayah calls the earth tractable and invites people to walk its reaches and eat its provision.
terra: The section joins looking, sky, and straight arrangement; this ayah asks whether people see the birds above them with wings spread (صَافَّاتٍ), a mobile aerial use of the same root.
terra: The prose hears living beings broadcast across the prepared earth; using a different verb, this ayah says God spread humankind throughout earth and will gather them to Him.

luna: The section shows earth and mountains fitted into place; here both are lifted and crushed with one blow, reversing their construction. | terra: The section composes earth and mountains as floor and pegs; this ayah has both carried up and crushed with one crushing, undoing the assembled pair together.
terra: The section's sky is a raised, stable roof; this ayah says the sky will split and become frail on that Day, reversing both its integrity and strength.
luna: The section's sky is a raised roof; here on the Day of Judgment the sky is like molten metal, a specific change of the overhead scene.

luna: The section's source dictionary links earth-coverings with wool; here mountains are like carded wool, الْعِهْنِ, as their firm form unravels. | terra: The section connects mountains with rugs and wool through the world's furnishings; this ayah turns the mountains into tufts of wool, dissolving rigid pegs into textile-like matter.

terra: The prose's نصب is an upright set object; this ayah likens people rushing from graves to a marker or cult-stone toward which they race, preserving that concrete set-up sense in a different scene.

luna: The sky is made in seven layers, طِبَاقًا; this supplies another image of a deliberately constructed canopy. | terra: The section asks people to look at how the sky was raised; Noah likewise asks whether they have seen how God created seven heavens in layers.
terra: After 71:15's layered heavens, this ayah places the moon within them as light and the sun as a lamp, adding illumination to the section's roof-like sky.

luna: The section's image of the earth as a spread covering is stated here as Allah making the earth بِسَاطًا, a carpet or broad spread. | terra: The section's earth is a rug-like spread beneath the world's tent; Noah tells his people here that God made the earth for them as a carpet (بِسَاطًا).
luna: After 71:19 calls earth a carpet, this ayah says people travel along its broad roads; the spread surface is made usable for movement.

luna: The section's mountains are planted supports; here earth and mountains shake and the mountains become shifting sand dunes, reversing that stability. | terra: The section's upright mountains peg a level earth; this ayah makes earth and mountains quake until the mountains become a loose heap of sand.
terra: Like the section's sequence from creation to making straight, this ayah says that God created the human being and then proportioned him.
terra: The section's cups are part of the Garden's prepared hospitality; this ayah says the righteous drink from a cup whose mixture is camphor, specifying what such a vessel bears.

luna: Garden dwellers recline on couches under protection from sun and cold; this situates couches as the section's sheltered room furnishings. | terra: The section's furnished Garden room is a place of rest; this ayah places its people reclining there on couches, sheltered from harsh sun and cold.

luna: Silver vessels and cups are carried around to the garden dwellers; this is a direct counterpart to the section's placed cups. | terra: The section describes cups set in an ordered room; this ayah has silver vessels and crystal cups circulated around the Garden-dwellers.

luna: The section names cups among measured furnishings; this verse says the cups are made to a measured size, قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا. | terra: The prose says the maker's work begins in exact measure; this ayah describes the Garden's silver crystal vessels as measured with precise measure (قَدَّرُوهَا تَقْدِيرًا).
terra: The section's placed cup is here filled with a ginger mixture and served in the Garden, another concrete use of the prepared vessel.
terra: The section raises the sky as an intact canopy; this ayah marks the promised Day by that sky being opened or rent apart.

luna: The section shows mountains set upright in the world's design; this Judgment scene says they are blown away. | terra: The section's mountains are deliberately set upright; this ayah marks the promised Day by their being uprooted and blown away.
terra: The section moves from placing objects in a room to measured creation; this ayah places the human drop in a firm lodging, the womb, within the measuring sequence completed in 77:23.
terra: After the drop is lodged for a known term, this ayah says that God measured and is the excellent measurer, directly restating the craft principle developed in the section.
terra: The section makes earth the containing floor of the common dwelling; this ayah asks whether God made it a gathering container, with 77:26 specifying the living and dead whom it contains.
terra: After 77:25-26 makes earth a container, this ayah places lofty firm mountains in it and gives fresh water, another compact floor-and-pegs construction.

luna: The earth is made a bed, مِهَادًا; this is a direct counterpart to the section's level, laid-out world. | terra: The section's flattened earth is the spread floor of the world; this ayah asks whether God made the earth a resting bed (مِهَادًا).

luna: The mountains are made pegs, أَوْتَادًا; this directly names the same support image the section develops for mountains in the earth. | terra: The prose defines mountains as the earth's great pegs; this ayah states the same domestic-cosmic image by calling the mountains pegs (أَوْتَادًا).

luna: The sky above is built as seven strong structures; it extends the section's raised world canopy into a constructed ceiling. | terra: The room-world has a strong raised ceiling; this ayah describes seven strong structures built above its hearers.
terra: After 78:12 builds seven strong structures above, this ayah places a blazing lamp there, making the constructed cosmic ceiling into a furnished and illuminated one.

luna: The section's mountains are fixed and upright; here they are set moving until they become a mirage, سَرَابًا. | terra: Within the same surah that calls the mountains pegs in 78:7, this ayah makes them move away until they are a mirage, explicitly reversing their apparent stability.
terra: The section's placed cups belong to Garden provision; this ayah names a brimming cup within its parallel list of Garden rewards.

luna: The section's root ص ف ف links furnishings to straight rows; here the Spirit and angels stand in ranks, صَفًّا, on the appointed day. | terra: The section's line arranges the room; this ayah arranges the Spirit and angels standing in a row on the Day, shifting the same straight order to the heavenly assembly.

luna: Before 79:28 says the sky's height was raised and proportioned, this ayah asks whether human creation or the sky is harder and says He built it; it emphasizes the sky as a constructed work. | terra: The section treats the sky as a constructed roof; this ayah asks whether human creation is harder or the sky which God built, beginning the construction sequence continued in 79:28-32.

luna: The verse says the sky's height was raised and then proportioned, رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا; it directly joins the section's lifting and measured shaping. | terra: The section cites the raised sky as a ceiling made even; this ayah names both acts, raising its canopy and proportioning it (رَفَعَ سَمْكَهَا فَسَوَّاهَا).

luna: After 79:28 raises and proportions the sky, this ayah describes the earth spread out, دَحَاهَا, completing the paired roof-and-floor scene. | terra: In the sequence begun at 79:27, this ayah adds the earth spread out after the sky, matching the section's movement from raised ceiling to laid ground.
terra: Within the construction sequence of 79:27-32, this ayah brings water and pasture out of the spread earth, showing the leveled floor made habitable rather than merely shaped.
terra: In the same construction sequence, this ayah says God anchored the mountains, matching the section's mountains erected as the world's pegs.
terra: After sky, earth, water, pasture, and mountains are prepared in 79:27-32, this ayah calls them provision for people and their livestock, reconnecting the built world to the section's camel.
terra: The prose explains creation through prior measurement; this ayah says that God created the human being from a drop and then determined his measure or course.

luna: The section's mountain supports appear set in place; here the mountains are set in motion on the Day the created order is transformed. | terra: The section asks how mountains were erected; this ayah marks the Last Day by their being set in motion, the opposite of fixed upright placement.
terra: The section reads the sky as the roof covering the world-room; this ayah has that covering stripped away.
terra: The section's raised sky forms a whole ceiling; this ayah opens the Last-Day scene with that sky split apart.

luna: The section's dictionary reading of خَلَقَ includes measuring material to fit; here Allah says He created, proportioned, and balanced the human form, خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّاكَ فَعَدَلَكَ. | terra: The section explicitly extends its craft image to the human body; this ayah joins creating, proportioning, and balancing the addressee.

luna: This ayah continues the proportioned form of 82:7 by saying Allah assembled a person in whichever form He willed; it extends the section's measured making to chosen shape. | terra: After 82:7 names creating, proportioning, and balancing, this ayah says that God assembled the human being in whatever form He willed, adding construction from parts to the craft sequence.

luna: The garden dwellers recline on couches and look out; this repeats the section's furniture in a setting of settled ease. | terra: The section moves from looking at creation to raised Garden seating; this ayah unites repose and vision as the righteous look out from couches.

luna: The righteous again sit on couches and look out; the repeated scene reinforces the couch as a feature of the garden setting. | terra: This repeated scene again has the blessed looking from couches, echoing both the section's furnishing and its command to see what has been made.
terra: The section sees the sky as a raised, intact ceiling; this ayah opens the final scene with that sky split apart, before 84:3 stretches out the earth below.

luna: The section treats earth as a spread floor; here the earth is stretched out at the Judgment, a boundary where its settled form changes. | terra: The section's earth is deliberately leveled as the world's floor; in the scene begun at 84:1, this ayah stretches it out at the Judgment, a final and destructive counterpart to its first preparation.

luna: The section cites this wording, خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ, as creation followed by setting in order; it gives the room and world parallel a compact Qur'anic formulation. | terra: The section explicitly invokes this formulation to ground all four making gestures in order: the Creator creates and then makes proportionate (خَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ).

luna: After 87:2 says creation is set in order, this ayah says Allah measured and guided it, قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ; it makes the section's measure-before-fitting theme explicit. | terra: Immediately after the creation and proportioning cited from 87:2, this ayah adds determining measure and guiding; it completes the section's claim that making something fit begins in measure.
luna: The section presents earth as a fitted floor; here earth is pounded flat and pulverized, ending that stable arrangement.

luna: The section's root ص ف ف describes ordered rows; here angels arrive rank upon rank, صَفًّا صَفًّا, on the Day of Judgment. | terra: The repeated phrase row upon row (صَفًّا صَفًّا) makes the angelic arrival an ordered array, a solemn counterpart to the section's repeated arrangement of objects.

luna: The oath names the sky and its builder; this echoes the section's sky as a constructed roof. | terra: The section hears architecture in the raised sky; this oath names the sky and the One who built it, making construction the act by which the cosmos appears.

luna: The oath names the earth and the One who spread it, طَحَاهَا; it repeats the section's image of a laid-out ground. | terra: The section's last hand movement is making the earth an even spread; this oath names the earth and the One who spread it out.
luna: After sky-building and earth-spreading in 91:5–6, this ayah says the soul was proportioned, سَوَّاهَا; it extends the section's ordered creation theme to a living form.
terra: The section finds uprightness and right measure beneath creation; this ayah locates human creation in the finest configuration (أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ).
luna: The section's world has a level, laid-out earth; here the earth is shaken with its final convulsion, a direct reversal of the floor's stability.
luna: After the shaking of 99:1, the earth casts out its burdens; this continues the rupture of the section's settled, furnishing surface.

luna: The section's root reading of ب ث ث describes rugs spread out; here people are scattered like moths, الْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ, turning a laid-out covering into a dispersed Judgment scene. | terra: The prose explicitly contrasts carpets spread in the Garden with people scattered on that Day; this ayah makes the people like dispersed moths (الْفَرَاشِ الْمَبْثُوثِ).

luna: The section's dictionary entry says a thick rug may be made of wool; here mountains become carded wool, الْعِهْنِ الْمَنفُوشِ, so the planted landscape unravels into textile-like matter. | terra: Beside the dispersed people of 101:4, the erected mountains become carded wool here; the world's pegs turn into the same soft textile register as its rugs.
